answer: When identity creation spikes, the network raises the proof-of-work required for every new identity, like a river narrowing into a canyon during a flood: a lone traveler can still pass, but an army of clones must pay a steep toll for each crossing. The difficulty only falls again after the meadow of fresh registrations thins out, so a Sybil attacker faces exponentially rising costs per identity while honest newcomers simply wait for calmer water.
